decisions.quote: This replication shows that the apparent gap growth in the Great Equalizer study was an artifact of scaling. When we measure reading and math ability with something closer to a vertical interval scale, gaps grow very little. While the contrast between school and summer still suggests that schools do something to equalize children, the amount of equalization now seems rather small compared to the inequality that exists at the start of kindergarten.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly present their findings as a partial correction of Downey et al. (2004): the original conclusion of substantial inequality growth after kindergarten entry fails to replicate once scaling artifacts are removed, whereas the seasonal finding that schools reduce inequality relative to summer vacation is partially supported.
